description: Irish residential heating demand profiles is a data set deposited in Mendeley Data by its authors John Curtis, Niall Farrell (Economic and Social Research Institute). This dataset contains information on residential heating system operation in Ireland. The dataset is drawn from high frequency smart thermostats that record internal temperature, set-point values, and boiler operation data approximately every three minutes. The data covers a period of 24 months from 1 October 2019 until 30 September 2021 from 9,815 separate properties. Coverage: national (IE); the metadata date the deposit to 2024. The formats are not stated in the metadata. It is reached through its DOI or landing page, listed on this page. Access is free of charge and open according to the repository. The licence is CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: written from the DataCite metadata (title, abstract, subjects and rights) read on 2026-09-29; the deposit itself was not opened or downloaded, so its contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support power-system, energy-planning and grid-operation studies. Related record: the repository-level record data-mendeley-repository.
